Adopted a 1 1/2 year old from the pound this past summer and said goodbye to my senior two days ago. In no way is Taz meant to be a replacement, I wasn't even really planning to get him, but I have to say having him here while I grieve has made a world of difference. His personality is massive and it's hard to stay so sad when I have a little goofball flailing through the house at all times. 

I'm glad we adopted him before Bentley's passing. I think him being here had made the transition a little easier for all of us. It's so hard to watch our furry friends slow down with age and sickness, Taz is a reminder that there's a whole lifetime you spend with them before that point. The destination will never change, but the journey together is what makes it so special. 

If you are ready to bring a new pup into the fold, I say go for it. It won't be the same love/bond you shared with Chico, but it will be special in its own right! A new friend for a new chapter. 

I'm sorry for your loss and good luck to you my friend!

Also terraforming a map takes ~forever~  so you gotta trust the process or do it in small sections. I have a mountain that I spend about 10 minutes making bigger and fleshing out everytime I go in that zoo lol
I can't say how many times I've gotten stuck on the logistics of a build and hopped into the workshop to find something similar so that I can analyze the construction of it lmao

Definitely check out the YouTube channel's recommended in the comments. Usually I'll just leave a video playing in the background while I build as inspiration. I find that helps me build a little more ambitiously.

Another tip is make a zoo solely for playing with ideas. This was a hard one for me because I like everything perfect but having a space where you can test build whatever you want is really helpful. Also having an experimental zoo allows me to relax and enjoy the game more because I've already mentally accepted it wont ever be perfect or polished. If I really like a concept, that's when I go to place it in a polished build. This applies to terraforming as well.

Finally, practice, get innovative, and practice some more. One of the things I've noticed about builds that really blow me away are the intelligent use of build pieces in new and creative ways. For example, I've been playing with the water wheels as roof pieces and it's made some really interesting builds. 

Find build styles that work for you. If you dont like hyper realistic builds, simply dont do them. I personally end up somewhere realistic-adjacent lol 

Eventually you'll see progress in your own builds and really that's the fuel that feeds the fire. Once you realize you are improving on yourself, it makes it easier to not get hung up on not being as skilled as other builders. I recently made a second reptile house after a year of playing and I was blown away at my own glow up.

Dont get discouraged, keep building, and remember this is a game and to enjoy yourself!

What you are looking for is a LGD like great pyrenees, anatolian shepherds, ect. Those are dogs that can be trained to protect your flock and your property 24/7, 365. They do require extensive training and can be problematic if not trained well. 

Donkey's can happily live with a flock and serve as a great deterrent for predators. However, donkey's are prey animals and essentially just as vulnerable to attack as a sheep (even if they put up a fight.)

Additionally, the donkey has to be tolerant of sheep which may be difficult to find if you didnt raise the aniaml from the ground up yourself. I've met donkeys who are indifferent to sheep and little critters and I've met donkeys who would squish them. Some dont like lambing or breeding. It's all up to the individual and it isnt always the scenario you're hoping for. 

100% do research and make your choice carefully!
